relations.subject: n1ql:insert
relations.evidence:
The INSERT statement fails if a document with the same document key already exists in the keyspace.

To insert documents into a keyspace and replace any existing documents with the same key, use the UPSERT statement.

relations.subject: n1ql:insert
relations.evidence: You can also insert documents by merging: in other words, by joining one data source to another, and inserting documents that do not match.

notable_absence.finding: Unlike cloud/n1ql/n1ql-language-reference/insert.json (which carries privilege:capella-basic-access-write, privilege:capella-advanced-access-query-insert etc.), this guide page never states which privilege or credential type is required to run INSERT/UPSERT/MERGE - the whole access-control axis is omitted from the task-oriented rewrite, exactly as with the KV-operation guides in this batch.

cross_component_finding: This page is a clean confirmation of the round's hypothesis: it reuses n1ql:insert, n1ql:upsert, and n1ql:merge without adding any new statement-level concept, and every worked example explicitly defers detail ('For more information and examples, see...') back to the cloud/n1ql/n1ql-language-reference/ pages rather than restating their content - no inconsistent-wording duplication found. The one addition specific to guide-level content is procedural framing not present on the reference pages: numbered how-to steps like 'Use the INTO keyword to specify the keyspace...' walking through clause order, which is task guidance rather than a new concept.
